risks: Eight named people are visible by the end of chapter3. Chapter4 should not introduce another cluster of four or five named recurring characters.
Chapter2 must remain ordinary in later callbacks. Do not retroactively narrate the trip as the origin of a professionally decisive Song-Xu relationship.
Xu Hang appears in both chapter1 and chapter2; this is useful connective tissue but must not accidentally make him look like the hidden central node of the ensemble.
The nine-month jump into chapter3 needs a light date/season marker in final manuscript layout; prose should not explain the intervening history just to smooth chronology.
The opening currently privileges educated professional problems. Before the first major arc accelerates, later chapters need bodily, domestic, financial and ordinary institutional texture as well.
continuity_rules_forward: For chapters4-6, prefer returning already introduced names over introducing many new recurring characters.
A newly introduced recurring person should get one concrete behavioral handle, not a paragraph biography.
Do not remind readers of every prior relation when a person reappears; let context reactivate memory.
Keep chapter2 consequences sparse: acquaintance may persist without becoming leverage.
Preserve chronological gaps as gaps unless a later scene genuinely needs an intervening fact.
next_step: Update Storyteller head and choose chapter4 with a bias toward returning characters and a different pressure register.
